claims.text: Slight compositional tuning of FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers can induce stress-activated martensitic transformation or twin formation at their interfaces during sustained tensile loading.
The interfacial transformation progressively accommodates plastic deformation.
Transformation-mediated deformation can occur without a catastrophic loss of strength.
The untuned, as-deposited multilayers possess a stable nanoscale FCC/BCC multilayer architecture.
Small compositional changes in one or both layers can lower the stress threshold for interfacial transformation.
Martensitic transformation or twin formation can be activated between room temperature and 300 °C without causing premature failure.
Optimized compositional tuning causes deformation twins and/or martensitic regions to nucleate and grow near FCC/BCC interfaces.
The tuned composition locally reduces the energy barrier for interfacial transformation under sustained stress.
Martensitic regions or twins provide new pathways for dislocation motion.
The evolving martensitic regions or twins progressively absorb strain energy.
The evolving interfacial structures smooth plastic deformation while retaining overall strength.
Relative to the untuned baseline, the tuned multilayer will exhibit a delayed and gradual onset of transformation at a critical stress.
The fraction of twin boundaries or martensitic regions will increase with progressive plastic strain.
Increasing transformation-feature fraction will produce a smoother and more controlled stress-strain response.
Untuned FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers do not exhibit progressive transformation under comparable loading.
The proposed mechanism remains effective only where thermal activation supports but does not overwhelm transformation kinetics, nominally up to about 300 °C.
Above about 300 °C, thermal softening or excessive transformation may cause behavior to deviate from the prediction.
Analogous systems support a qualitative relationship between compositional tuning and progressive transformation.

contradictions.description: The intervention is said to lower the transformation stress threshold, but the predicted outcome calls transformation delayed relative to a baseline that is separately said not to transform progressively at all. The reference point for 'delayed' is therefore internally unclear and may oppose the claimed threshold reduction.
